sources.citation: Glottolog 5.1. Languoid kurr1245 'Kur'; reference records 43011 (Collins 1982) and 152212 (Loski & Loski 1989).

Zero grammar/phonology/sketch references; the five listed items are two von Rosenberg overviews, Collins 1982 (subclassification comment cites pp. 122-123), Loski & Loski 1989 (overview/comparative, covers c. 43 East Seram varieties incl. Teor and Kur), and the Ribbe 1903 wordlist.

sources.citation: Grimes, Charles E. & Owen Edwards. 2026. The Austronesian languages of eastern Indonesia and Timor-Leste: Unravelling their prehistory and classification. Berlin: Language Science Press. Section 11.4 'Teor-Kur', pp. 464-468 (open access, Zenodo 18323007).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. Section 11.4 is historical phonology (sound correspondences) only. p. 464: 'Data is extremely scarce for both languages.. The only data for Kur we have been able to access is the word list in von Rosenberg (1867: 108-114), as well as two folktales, Ohoiwutun (2021) and Rado (2021), published by the Indonesian language office.' Kur forms are cited from the booklets in Indonesian orthography with no prosodic marking; no stress or accent remark anywhere in the section.

sources.citation: Wikipedia (en). 'Teor-Kur language' (redirect target of 'Kur language'), accessed 2026-09-17.
sources.note: Nothing; classification and speaker numbers only, references limited to Ethnologue and Grimes & Edwards 2026.

sources.citation: Hughes, Jock. 1987. The languages of Kei, Tanimbar and Aru: a lexicostatistic classification. NUSA 27: 71-111. Section 2.1.2.2 'Teor-Kur', p. 84.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing (as recorded in the sibling teor1240 check, which scanned and read the section): only segmental dialect notes, Kur word-final alveolars correspond to Ut palatals, Kur velar nasals to Ut voiced velar plosives. No stress/accent in the paper.

sources.citation: Ribbe, Carl. 1903. 68 Woerter in 34 verschiedenen Sprachen und Dialekten der Sued-See, der papuanischen und der malayischen Inseln. In Zwei Jahre unter den Kannibalen der Salomo-Inseln, 196-212. Dresden: Elbgau (archive.org zweijahreunterd01kalbgoog).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. The table has a 'Koor' column (68 unaccented forms, e.g. nongbie, menrana, memvina, bobobor, tata, inan); no accent marks and no note on stress. The only pronunciation note (p. 184) concerns the vowels of the Shortlands (Alu) language.

sources.citation: von Rosenberg, C. B. H. 1878. Der Malayische Archipel: Land und Leute in Schilderungen. Leipzig: Gustav Weigel. 'b. Die Inseln Koor und Tijoor' pp. 352-355; 'II. Vergleichendes Woerterverzeichniss' pp. 597 ff., column 13 Koor (archive.org dermalayischearc00rose).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. a full-text search for stress/accent/Betonung/Aussprache/Tonzeichen gives no hits in the whole book; the Koor section (pp. 352-355) is ethnographic (population c. 100 in Kilmas, Muslim, Bandanese origin tradition); the wordlist table scanned is garbled, and per Grimes & Edwards 2026 fn. 13 it is only a re-orthographised copy of the 1867 list.

sources.citation: von Rosenberg, C. B. H. 1867. Reis naar de zuidoostereilanden, gedaan in 1865. 's Gravenhage: Martinus Nijhoff. Vergelijkende woordenlijst, Koor column, pp. 108-114; notes pp. 105-107 (archive.org reis-naar-de-zuidoostereilanden).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on stress. p. 107 transcription note only: 'is gebruik gemaakt van de accenten der fransche taal boven de e.. en van de teekens [breve] om aan te toonen dat eene lettergreep kort en [macron] dat zij lang is' (accents mark vowel quality of e and syllable quantity, not stress). p. 106 note on Koor: the small resident population descends from emigrated Bandanese, so its dialect resembles Eli-Ellat (Banda); no accent marks for stress in the Koor column.
